title: Jellyfin playback
description: Where video playback is bottlenecked, hop by hop and per path, for one Jellyfin instance (kube-cluster/apps/jellyfin README, "Playback dashboard").

list.description: The kube worker running the selected instance's pod.

list.label: HLS segment length (s)

options.content:
Top row: the outcome first (**pace**: content seconds fetched per wall second per stream, below 1 the buffer drains), then **transcode speed**, which tells an encoder at its limit (near 1) from serving or delivery (well above 1), then the verdict. A tile counts only while its path is active for the selected instance, else *idle*. Green, yellow, red is against what one stream needs; each tile's description says what it includes.

- **Direct play**: Jellyfin streams the file itself.
- **ffmpeg path**: every remux and transcode; ffmpeg runs on the GPU worker, Jellyfin serves its HLS segments from the transcode dir.

**Not separable: segment serving and delivery.** No metric ends at the first byte; most of a slow segment is Jellyfin's wait before it. *Delivery share* and *Segments over 4.1 s* are context.

panels.title: Worst stage now
panels.description: ffmpeg path, judged by pace (content seconds fetched per wall second per HLS session). Pace 0.9 or more: ok. Below: transcode speed under 1.3 means the encoder is at its limit, named by its hottest stage past yellow (GPU host CPU, NVENC, NVDEC, GPU memory or power, HDD OSD mean); otherwise Jellyfin node CPU or the transcode-dir read if past yellow, else segment serving or delivery (mostly Jellyfin's wait before the first byte; speed far above 1, e.g. over 3, also fits a client that stopped fetching). Scored by pace: 1 at 0.9, 2 at 0.7. Direct play: the hottest of its stages. 0-1 ok, 1-2 watch, 2 and up bottleneck.

panels.title: Pace
panels.description: Content seconds fetched per wall second per HLS session: HLS segment rate x segment length / sessions (progress reports x 10 minus direct streams), 2 m window. Below 1 the player's buffer drains; above 1 it fills. Idle for the first 1-2 minutes of a session. A client that reports progress while paused reads as stalled. Yellow below 0.9, red below 0.7.

panels.title: Delivery share
panels.description: Context: mean time Jellyfin takes per HLS segment request / segment length. Most of it is Jellyfin's wait before the first byte, not the download, and a session's first segment (25-40 s on a 4K source) lifts it for 5 minutes, so it is not a verdict input.

panels.title: Segments over 4.1 s
panels.description: Context: share of HLS segment requests slower than 4.096 s (a histogram bucket edge), the download included. Healthy and stalling sessions overlap here, so it has no threshold.

panels.title: Transcode speed
panels.description: Estimate: ffmpeg's write rate on docker-d / the instance's Traefik bytes out, so it floors near 1 when the encoder limits and the player keeps up. It is the verdict's classifier, not an outcome: with pace low, below 1.3 means the encoder is the limit, well above 1 means serving, delivery or a client not fetching. Under-reads while a player fills its buffer; counts every ffmpeg on the shared GPU host.

panels.title: HLS sessions
panels.description: Playback progress reports x 10 (clients report every ~10 s, paused ones too) minus direct streams, 2 m window: the remuxes and transcodes of the selected instance. Unlike the segment rate it stays up while a player stalls.

panels.title: Stages over time
panels.description: The verdict's stages, one row each, coloured like the tiles while their path was active, empty while idle. Pace is the outcome; Transcode speed is red while pace is low and speed is below 1.3 (the encoder limits). Trace a past stall to the rows that were red.

panels.title: Standing probe (jellyfin-sqlite, every 6 h; skipped while anyone streams)
Probe pace
panels.description: Content seconds played per wall second after startup, last probe run per mode: 1 without stalls. Yellow below 0.9, red below 0.7.

panels.title: Probe startup
panels.description: From PlaybackInfo to 3 s buffered, last run per mode. A 4K transcode takes 25-40 s, most of it ffmpeg probing the source.

panels.title: Probe segment TTFB
panels.description: Time to first byte of the HLS segments after the first, last transcode run: p50 and p95. Mostly Jellyfin's wait before it serves a segment ffmpeg has long written.

panels.title: Probe runs (7 d)
panels.description: Runs by result over 7 days: ok, skipped (someone streamed or ffmpeg ran) and error (see the CronJob's pod log).

panels.title: Direct play: client ← cluster Traefik ← Jellyfin ← CephFS media mount ← HDD OSDs
Direct streams
panels.description: Direct-play requests of the selected instance in flight (max over 5 min). Zero: idle.

panels.title: CephFS media read
panels.description: Average read latency of the kernel client of the media mount (PV jellyfin-media-stream on $node), network and OSD queues included; both instances share it when they run on one node. The mount reads ahead 64 MiB, 16 objects of 4 MiB in flight, which a 4K remux at 10 MB/s drains in about 6.5 s: a read slower than that stalls the stream. Yellow 2 s, red 6 s. Not backtested: infra/cephfs-client-metrics is new.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(cephfs_client_latency_seconds_total{pv="jellyfin-media-stream", node="$node", op="read"}[5m])) / sum(rate(cephfs_client_ops_total{pv="jellyfin-media-stream", node="$node", op="read"}[5m]))) and on() ((sum(max_over_time(http_requests_in_progress{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetVideoStream|GetVideoStreamByContainer|GetAudioStream|GetAudioStreamByContainer|GetUniversalAudioStream"}[5m]))) > 0)

panels.title: Jellyfin node CPU
panels.description: CPU busy on the kube worker running the selected instance's pod ($node), every pod on it included; counts for direct play and, past yellow, in the ffmpeg verdict. Yellow 80%, red 95%.

panels.title: Jellyfin node NIC
panels.description: Busier direction of $node's VM NIC (Proxmox), in Mbit/s. Carries client traffic and the CephFS reads. Not in the verdict: Proxmox reports no link speed.

panels.title: HDD OSD read latency
panels.description: Read-weighted mean latency of all HDD OSDs (network and queue included), with the slowest OSD (reads of at least 0.05/s) below it as context: one slow OSD showed 2.8 s while a direct-play client read without a blocked read. The archive pool lives on the HDDs, but no metric maps a pool to its OSDs. Yellow 2 s, red 6 s, the readahead budget of the CephFS media tile. Both paths read the source from this pool.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"})) / sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))) and on() (((sum(max_over_time(http_requests_in_progress{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetVideoStream|GetVideoStreamByContainer|GetAudioStream|GetAudioStreamByContainer|GetUniversalAudioStream"}[5m]))) > 0) or ((sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetHlsVideoSegment|GetHlsAudioSegment|GetHlsVideoSegmentLegacy|GetHlsAudioSegmentLegacy"}[5m])) * ${segment_s}) > 0))

max(((sum by (ceph_daemon) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[5m])) / (sum by (ceph_daemon) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[5m])) > 0.05)) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))) and on() (((sum(max_over_time(http_requests_in_progress{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetVideoStream|GetVideoStreamByContainer|GetAudioStream|GetAudioStreamByContainer|GetUniversalAudioStream"}[5m]))) > 0) or ((sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetHlsVideoSegment|GetHlsAudioSegment|GetHlsVideoSegmentLegacy|GetHlsAudioSegmentLegacy"}[5m])) * ${segment_s}) > 0))

panels.title: ffmpeg path (remux and transcode): Jellyfin → SSH → GPU worker on docker-d → transcode dir → Jellyfin
CephFS transcode-dir read
panels.description: Read latency of the pod's kernel client on the selected instance's transcode dir (PV <instance>-transcodes on $node), waiting for the worker's caps included: Jellyfin serves the segments the GPU worker wrote there. A segment is 3 s: yellow 0.5 s, red 1.5 s. In the ffmpeg verdict once past yellow.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(cephfs_client_latency_seconds_total{pv="${instance:text}-transcodes", node="$node", op="read"}[5m])) / sum(rate(cephfs_client_ops_total{pv="${instance:text}-transcodes", node="$node", op="read"}[5m]))) and on() ((sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetHlsVideoSegment|GetHlsAudioSegment|GetHlsVideoSegmentLegacy|GetHlsAudioSegmentLegacy"}[5m])) * ${segment_s}) > 0)

panels.title: GPU host NIC
panels.description: Busier direction of docker-d's VM NIC (Proxmox), in Mbit/s: the worker's CephFS reads of the source come in, the segments it writes to the transcode dir go out. Not in the verdict: Proxmox reports no link speed.

panels.title: Source read (ffmpeg)
panels.description: ffmpeg's read rate on docker-d, the CephFS source over the network included, and the HDD OSDs' read-weighted mean latency (yellow 2 s, red 6 s). Approximates the CephFS client on this host, which has no exporter.

targets.expr: ((sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"})) / sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[5m]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"})))) and on() ((sum(rate(http_requests_received_total{app_kubernetes_io_name="${instance:text}", action=~"GetHlsVideoSegment|GetHlsAudioSegment|GetHlsVideoSegmentLegacy|GetHlsAudioSegmentLegacy"}[5m])) * ${segment_s}) > 0)

panels.title: Gap: CephFS on the GPU host

options.content: docker-d runs no CephFS exporter (`infra/cephfs-client-metrics` covers the kube workers only), so the source read there has no latency of its own. *Source read* approximates it: ffmpeg's read rate plus the HDD OSD mean.

panels.title: GPU host CPU
panels.description: ffmpeg's CPU on docker-d as a share of the host's logical CPUs (the big number), and in cores. Software decode and filters land here; other processes on the host are not counted. Yellow 80%, red 95%.

panels.title: NVENC
panels.description: Encoder utilization of the Quadro P2200, shared by both workers. NVIDIA lists no session limit for Quadro cards, so the encoder engine itself is the limit. 5-minute mean: a 60 s sample of the bursty engine swings from 0 to 0.9 within one healthy stream. Yellow 70%, red 90%.

panels.title: NVDEC
panels.description: Decoder utilization of the P2200. 5-minute mean: a 60 s sample of the bursty engine swings from 0 to 0.9 within one healthy stream. Yellow 70%, red 90%.

panels.title: GPU memory
panels.description: Used of the P2200's 5 GiB; when full, new sessions fail to start. Yellow 80%, red 95%.

panels.title: GPU power / limit
panels.description: Power draw against the board limit (75 W). At the limit the clocks drop: a throttling hint. Yellow 85%, red 97%.

panels.title: Bytes to clients
panels.description: Response bytes/s. Cluster Traefik per route of the selected instance (HLS only: a direct-play range stream closed by the client is recorded with no bytes), the Jellyfin pod's network transmit (direct play included, plus the SSH session to the GPU worker), and the edge line, all cluster traffic (the edge forwards everything to one service, so it cannot be split per app).

panels.title: Average request time per hop
panels.description: Average request time at the edge (all cluster traffic), the cluster Traefik and Jellyfin (selected instance). Not hop delay: the request sets differ, and long streams and websockets dominate each average as they end. A hop that adds whole seconds still shows as a gap.

panels.title: HLS segment time
panels.description: Time Jellyfin takes per HLS segment request, against the segment length (red dashed). A segment slower than its length stalls playback.

panels.title: Sessions by path
panels.description: Direct-play requests in flight; ffmpeg sessions as progress reports x 10 minus those (what the HLS sessions tile shows); the segment rate x length as a cross-check, which falls while a player stalls.

panels.title: Requests by Jellyfin action
panels.description: Top 10 actions of the selected instance by request rate, probes excluded.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: 5xx answers per second at the cluster Traefik for the selected instance, and Jellyfin's own 5xx.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: The selected instance's pod in cores, and its node's CPU busy (right axis).

panels.title: Pod network
panels.description: The pod's own traffic: clients and the SSH session to the GPU worker. CephFS reads are the node kernel's and are not in it (see Node NIC).

panels.title: Node NIC
panels.description: The VM NIC of $node from Proxmox (in-guest counters on the kube workers only see the collector pod's network namespace). Includes the CephFS kernel client.

panels.title: Pod memory
panels.description: Working set of the selected instance's pod; the limit is 4 GiB.

panels.title: Storage: CephFS clients, archive pool, OSDs
CephFS client read latency
panels.description: Kernel clients of the media mount and of the selected instance's transcode dir, per node. Reconstructed from the kernel's lifetime average, so noisy with few reads (infra/cephfs-client-metrics).

targets.expr: sum by (pv, node) (rate(cephfs_client_latency_seconds_total{pv=~"jellyfin-media-stream|${instance:text}-transcodes", op="read"}[5m])) / sum by (pv, node) (rate(cephfs_client_ops_total{pv=~"jellyfin-media-stream|${instance:text}-transcodes", op="read"}[5m]))

panels.title: CephFS client requests
panels.description: Read and metadata requests per second on the same mounts. With 64 MiB readahead a media read is one object of up to 4 MiB. Read bytes are not shown: on kernel 6.12 they stay 0 on most mounts.

panels.title: Archive pool reads
panels.description: Client reads of the archive data pool (cephfs.archive.data, id 42), everyone's.

panels.title: Slowest 10 HDD OSDs
panels.description: Read latency per HDD OSD with at least 0.05 reads/s, and the read-weighted average of all HDD OSDs (dashed). A single OSD far above the average points at its disk; a whole host at the host.

targets.expr: topk(10, (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (ceph_daemon, hostname) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[$__rate_interval])) > 0.05)) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))

sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[$__rate_interval]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"})) / sum(rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[$__rate_interval]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))

panels.title: OSD read latency by host
panels.description: Read-weighted average over each Ceph host's HDD OSDs.

targets.expr: sum by (hostname) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum[$__rate_interval]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"})) / sum by (hostname) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_latency_count[$__rate_interval]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))

panels.title: OSD read throughput by host
panels.description: Bytes/s the HDD OSDs of each host return to clients.

targets.expr: sum by (hostname) (rate(ceph_osd_op_r_out_bytes[$__rate_interval]) * on (ceph_daemon) group_left () max by (ceph_daemon) (ceph_osd_metadata{device_class="hdd"}))

panels.title: ffmpeg path: GPU worker on docker-d
GPU engines
panels.description: Quadro P2200, shared by both workers (and anything else on the GPU).

panels.title: GPU memory and power
panels.description: Memory used against total, power draw against the limit (right axis).

panels.title: ffmpeg processes
panels.description: All ffmpeg processes on docker-d (both workers, one series): CPU in cores, and I/O as /proc/<pid>/io reports it. Reads are the transcode input and include CephFS: in a sampled transcode they matched the VM's network input (1.5 GB in the same 75 s). Writes are the segments. Gaps: no ffmpeg running.

panels.title: Worker containers CPU
panels.description: Cores used by each ffmpeg worker service (cAdvisor; the selected instance's is ${instance}), and the host's CPU busy (right axis).

panels.title: GPU host NIC
panels.description: docker-d's VM NIC from Proxmox: the worker's CephFS reads of the source come in here, the segments it writes to the transcode dir go out.

panels.title: Worker containers network
panels.description: The containers' own interfaces: the SSH session from Jellyfin. CephFS is the host kernel's and is not in it.
